claims.text: High-entropy alloys exhibit superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance compared with conventional structural alloys at elevated temperatures.
Stainless steels and titanium alloys are examples of conventional structural alloys relevant to the comparison.
High-entropy alloys possess complex microstructures and compositions.
The complex microstructure and composition of high-entropy alloys enhance their mechanical properties.
The complex microstructure and composition of high-entropy alloys enhance their corrosion resistance.
Multiple principal elements in high-entropy alloys produce a more stable oxide layer.
Multiple principal elements in high-entropy alloys reduce wear rates under tribological conditions.
High-entropy alloys have lower wear rates than conventional alloys under comparable elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
High-entropy alloys have lower corrosion rates than conventional alloys under comparable elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
Reduced wear and corrosion rates lead to longer service life.
The magnitude of improvement varies with the specific high-entropy-alloy composition and environmental factors.
